page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 shared physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-micro in the bottom 10% across all tested performance metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU score is 132.9, and the multi-core score is 171.0. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 9.73 GB/sec, dropping to 0.1 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and large block write bandwidth at 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 201.56 and 176.45 respectively, while static web serving throughput is limited to 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-micro represents a low-cost entry point designed for workloads with minimal resource requirements. Because it utilizes a shared physical core and lacks dedicated local storage, it is not suitable for sustained high-throughput computing or memory-intensive database operations. Appropriate workloads are limited to lightweight utility tasks, basic development environments, simple microservices, or low-traffic static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core virtual machine instance designed for low-resource utility workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, it provides 2 vCPUs sharing a fraction of a physical core, paired with 1.0 GB of system memory. The instance does not include local storage, GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance benchmarks, including stress-ng and Passmark, place this instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware, with a Passmark CPU score of 201.56 and a static web serving throughput of 0.17 GB/sec. Given its shared-core architecture and highly constrained memory bandwidth, the e2-micro is best suited for lightweight tasks such as basic microservices, development testing, or low-traffic static web hosting where cost efficiency is prioritized over raw performance.
